title: Why most bank AI pilots never reach production
linkedinPost:
88% of bank AI pilots never reach production.

Not because the model failed. Because the governance was never designed to follow it there.

5 of the 6 failure modes have nothing to do with the technology:

• Pilot governance never upgrades to production standards — it grows until it serves real customers with no regulatory documentation
• Sandbox data looks nothing like production data — real systems have exceptions pilots never face
• No monitoring plan — no one can prove it's working
• Business process not redesigned — efficiency claimed on paper, not realised
• No model methodology, no independent validation, no Article 12 logging

The EU AI Act's high-risk obligations are enforceable as of August 2, 2026. A pilot built without them cannot go to production without a rebuild.

What I would actually do:

• Audit every pilot against a 4-level Readiness Ladder before approving another PoC
• Wire Article 12 logging and DORA incident reporting into the same Supabase event log from day one
• Run a governance review when the pilot first touches real customers — not at go-live
• Set a Revenue Per Employee target before any use case receives a production budget

Revenue per employee doesn't move from AI in a sandbox. It moves from AI in production, doing real work, with outcomes measured.

Full piece + the Pilot-to-Production Readiness Ladder — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: Why do most bank AI pilots fail to reach production?

acceptedAnswer.text: The failure is almost never the model. 5 of the 6 most common failure modes are organisational: governance that never upgrades from pilot to production standards, data architecture mismatch between sandbox and real systems, no monitoring plan, business transformation not designed in, and regulatory documentation absent from the build scope. Banks that resolve these structurally — not as an afterthought — scale AI in regulated financial services at a measurably higher rate.

mainEntity.name: What governance does a bank need before deploying AI in production?

acceptedAnswer.text: At minimum: a documented model development methodology, independent validation, EU AI Act Article 12 logging for any Annex III use case, defined performance monitoring thresholds with remediation triggers, change management processes for model updates, and DORA-aligned incident reporting. The Pilot-to-Production Readiness Ladder structures this as 4 levels, each with a defined minimum governance state.

mainEntity.name: How does the EU AI Act affect AI pilot deployments in European banks?

acceptedAnswer.text: High-risk system obligations became fully enforceable on August 2, 2026. AI systems involved in credit scoring, KYC, AML decision support, or customer eligibility — all Annex III classifications — require documented methodology, independent validation, and Article 12 inference logging before production go-live. Pilots built without these requirements cannot be promoted without a rebuild.

mainEntity.name: What does a successful AI pilot-to-production transition in banking look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: JPMorgan Chase's 400+ production use cases and Commonwealth Bank's 20% fraud loss reduction are the reference points. Both share the same underlying decision: a production governance platform built first, with use cases deployed into it — not pilots promoted individually. The platform governs. The use cases follow.
